We got result from apply_template: a tuple of strings? It shows "(('COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1'),)". That seems to be a tuple containing a tuple of two SMILES: product? Actually applying retrosynthetic template to target yields precursors. So the result is a list of precursor SMILES pairs. It gave one pair: 'COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1' and 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1'. So first reaction splits target into two fragments: fragment A (maybe aromatic core) and fragment B (some side chain). Good.

Now we need to apply next template 1914394 to each fragment? The route must have at least 3 reactions using templates in order: 1914393, then 1914394, then 1914395. Likely each reaction further disconnections.

We need to propose a route: start from target, apply 1914393 to get two precursors. Then apply 1914394 to one of those precursors (maybe the fragment with amide). Then apply 1914395 to further break down.

We need to verify applicability of each template to the chosen precursor using check_smiles_reaction_template_matching maybe. But we can attempt apply_template and see results.

First, apply 1914394 to fragment A: 'COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1'.
